summary: This post analyzes potential price cycles in GameStop (GME) driven by settlement mechanics and proposes that financial system vulnerabilities enable hidden short positions. The author identifies three cycle types: monthly/quarterly Supplementary Liquidity Deposit (SLD) cycles, and T+21 and T+35 "calendar-day" cycles. The author then argues the DTCC/NSCC systems permit hiding of failed-to-deliver trades through exemptions and an "Obligation Warehouse," and speculates that a mandatory corporate event (stock split, merger) triggered by Ryan Cohen could force a short squeeze ("MOASS"). The author self-rates confidence in cycle claims as low to moderate (C+21: 3/10, C+35: 4.5/10) and explicitly disclaims key claims as unverified.

key_claims.claim: Claims that SLD (Supplementary Liquidity Deposit) cycles create predictable monthly and quarterly price movements in GME stocks.
key_claims.note: Pages 4-9. Author gives this 9/10 confidence. However, the SEC's October 2021 report on the January 2021 event found the run-up was driven by positive-sentiment retail buying, not settlement cycles. No regulator documented predictable SLD-driven price cycles materializing.

key_claims.claim: Claims that T+21 and T+35 calendar-day cycles generate significant, exploitable price movements in GME.
key_claims.note: Pages 10-12. Author self-rates C+21 at 3/10 and admits 'C+21 is mostly horse shit' with effects 'close to invisible.' Author undermines the premise by Aug 2021.

key_claims.claim: Claims that DTCC/NSCC systems allow hiding of failed-to-deliver trades through CNS exemptions and Obligation Warehouse mechanisms.
key_claims.note: Pages 13-18. Author includes 'Big Fucking Warning' stating this is 'not 100% verified.' Author states 'Don't ask me for source. I can't give you shit.' Mechanisms are plausible but unverified speculation.

key_claims.claim: Claims that if Ryan Cohen executes a mandatory corporate event (stock split, merger), all hidden short obligations would be forced to close, triggering a squeeze (MOASS).
key_claims.note: Pages 17-18. GameStop executed a 4-for-1 stock split via dividend in July 2022. This mandatory corporate event did NOT trigger a squeeze. Core prediction is falsified by hindsight.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Robinhood's margin call on January 28, 2021, was the primary driver of GME price movement.
key_claims.note: Pages 8, 27. Margin call was real. SEC's October 2021 report confirmed positive-sentiment retail buying, not margin-call-driven short covering, was the primary driver. Margin calls were secondary.

key_claims.claim: Claims that GME can only stay alive through continuous ape purchases; without constant retail buying, the stock would die.
key_claims.note: Pages 9-10. GameStop returned to profitability in 2023-24, has diversified cash reserves, and added bitcoin to treasury by 2025. Company did not require constant retail cult buying to survive.

key_claims.claim: Claims that the DTCC operates vulnerable, outdated legacy systems with unfixed exploitable vulnerabilities.
key_claims.note: Pages 13-14. Author claims based on document review but states 'Don't ask me for source. I can't give you shit.' Unverified technical speculation, not audit or regulator finding.

validity_rationale: The core prediction (corporate event triggers MOASS) is falsified by the July 2022 stock split causing no squeeze. Cycle predictions are self-admitted ineffective by the author (C+21 'close to invisible'). Speculation dominates; FTD-hiding mechanisms are speculative interpretations, not verified facts. Multiple disclaimers indicate unverified claims.
